title: American Airlines 625
summary: American Airlines Flight 625, a Boeing 727-195, made an unstable approach to Cyril E. King Airport with maximum flap never applied. The aircraft floated due to wind conditions, touched down 2,300 feet down a 4,658-foot runway, and the captain rejected the landing too late. Engines responded slowly to go-around thrust commands. The aircraft overran the runway and struck a Shell gas station, killing 37 of 88 occupants.
probable_cause: The captain's failure to apply maximum flap setting during the approach in order to achieve the prescribed landing distance, failure to recognize the significance of the excessive speed and float characteristics of the aircraft, failure to execute a timely go-around when confronted with an unstable approach, and his subsequent panic in applying full brakes and reversers immediately before the impact. The captain's actions were compounded by his failure to use reverse thrust effectively during the landing roll. (p. 36-37)

factors.evidence: Aircraft approached with maximum flap setting of 40 degrees never applied, which meant aircraft speed was 10 knots higher than VREF. (p. 13)
Aircraft floated due to turbulent winds in the area, resulting in excessive ground speed on approach. (p. 13-14)
Captain did not have awareness that when he touched down 2,300 feet down the 4,658-foot runway, he did not have enough distance for a safe landing or go-around. (p. 14-15)
Pilot did not initiate go-around at a safe point; attempted go-around with only 700 feet remaining. After 5 seconds waiting for power, pilot panicked and applied full brakes. (p. 15)
Pilot forgot to apply reverse engine thrust until immediately before impact, severely reducing available stopping distance. (p. 15)
Aircraft ran off end of runway at high speed and struck Shell gas station located near the runway threshold. (p. 16)

events.text: American Airlines Flight 625 cleared for approach to runway 1 at Cyril E. King Airport
Aircraft in approach descent at excessive speed with maximum flap setting of 40 degrees never applied
Aircraft affected by turbulent wind conditions causing floating during descent; ground effect reduced effective landing distance
Aircraft touched down 2,300 feet down the 4,658-foot runway, with only approximately 2,358 feet remaining for stop
Captain applied full throttle to engines in go-around attempt 3 seconds after touchdown
After waiting 5 seconds for engine response, captain panicked and applied full wheel brakes and reversers
Aircraft overran runway end at high speed, approximately 160 knots, and struck Shell gas station
Aircraft came to rest against Shell gas station with fuselage extensively damaged; 37 of 88 occupants killed in post-crash fire

recommendations.text: Standardized procedures should require that landing calculations be made available to both pilots and reviewed before approach.
Approach stability criteria should be reviewed and procedures developed for mandatory go-around when approach becomes unstable.
Training programs should include specific procedures for recognition and response to unstable approaches and adequate go-around procedures.
Reverse thrust should be armed and ready prior to landing to allow immediate deployment when needed.
